drivers.variant_notes: Production ROM set (U1, U2, U5 and U6) and the reference for this definition: GEN_STMPU200, six-digit dispst6 displays, FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), Stern ST300 sound board. Every retained harness run except the clone solenoid test boots this driver.

Community seven-digit conversion, rev. 2. INITGAME differs from the production driver only in its display layout: seven-digit dispst7 player displays (segment starts 1, 9, 17 and 25) in place of dispst6. It needs seven-digit display hardware and otherwise keeps GEN_STMPU200, FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), the ST300 sound board and the same inputs. Its retained solenoid test fires the same nineteen outputs in the same order as the production ROM's.

Community seven-digit conversion with fixes and modified rules. INITGAME differs from the production driver only in its display layout: seven-digit dispst7 player displays (segment starts 1, 9, 17 and 25) in place of dispst6. It needs seven-digit display hardware and otherwise keeps GEN_STMPU200, FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), the ST300 sound board and the same inputs. The ROM was not available for a harness run.

Free-play build of the production ROM: the same U1 and U5 images with changed U2 and U6. Identical INITGAME data to the production driver (GEN_STMPU200, six-digit dispst6 displays, FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), no extra lamp columns, Stern ST300 sound board, input_ports_st), so the controller inventory is unchanged. No harness run was made with it.

Community rules change that replaces U6 only. Identical INITGAME data to the production driver (GEN_STMPU200, six-digit dispst6 displays, FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), no extra lamp columns, Stern ST300 sound board, input_ports_st), so the controller inventory is unchanged. The ROM was not available for a harness run.

physical.location: Inside the coin door
physical.notes: The Self-Test button inside the coin door (manual Figure 1), drawn on the cabinet sheet as `TEST SWITCH` from A4J3-1 (R) to A3J2-7 (Y-R). Public -7 drives the ROM's tests in the manual's order: in the retained runs the first press starts the burn-in, the fourth the solenoid test and the fifth the switch test.

physical.location: MPU module
physical.notes: PinMAME routes public -6 to the CPU's NMI line (BY35_SWCPUDIAG). The manual names no button for it; the S33 MEMORY CLEAR pushbutton is a separate contact (the remote memory-clear input), so the identity of the two is not assumed.

physical.location: Sound module
physical.notes: PinMAME routes public -5 to the ST300 sound board's diagnostic input (BY35_SWSOUNDDIAG). The manual documents no such button on the C-605 sound module.

physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `TOP RIGHT ROLL-OVER BUTTON`; matrix sheet: `TOP-R. R.O.W.`. Normally open contact with a series diode on the playfield wiring diagram. Star roll-over button right of the top lanes at the top of the shooter-lane return (location drawing leader 39 ends on a star). The Switch Identification table calls it a roll-over button, the matrix sheet repeats `TOP-R. R.O.W.` in its cell; the location drawing and the table model a star button, which is what the definition records. In the retained gameplay run, closed after the three top lanes, it lit the second A in the kicker lane (lamp 2, `"A"2 KICKER`), cleared the roll-over letter lamps and flickered the general-illumination relay (public 17). Placed on the retained table's Trigger `sw39`, which its script binds to this address.

physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `SAUCER`; matrix sheet: `SAUCER`. Normally open contact with a series diode on the playfield wiring diagram. Switch under the top eject pocket (location drawing leader 40). Held closed while a ball sits in it; the ROM scores the pocket and pulses public 8, the saucer eject, about three seconds after the closure (retained gameplay run). The pocket scores its lit value, advanced by the top thumper and the spinner. The manual says the value resets to 2,000 when the ball enters the out-hole; in the retained runs the ROM keeps the lit value from ball to ball (4,000 through the first drain and 6,000 through the second of the game-over run) and returns it to 2,000 only when the credit button starts a game. The ROM runs the rule either way, so a recreation inherits it. Placed on the retained table's Trigger `sw40`, which its script binds to this address.

mechanisms.behavior: Galaxy is a single-ball machine with no trough. The known-working script starts with the ball on the out-hole switch (public 33). When the credit button starts a game the ROM resets the drop-target bank (public 4) and kicks the out-hole (public 11, J-26-1000), repeating the kick for as long as public 33 stays closed; the retained runs show the repeats stop once 33 opens. The kick sends the ball to the shooter lane, where the player launches it with the plunger. After every drain the bonus is counted, the player and ball advance, and the kick repeats.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball out-hole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the top centre of the playfield (parts list `Saucer Eject` J-28-2300). A ball in it holds public 40 closed; the ROM scores the pocket's lit value and pulses public 8 about three seconds after the closure, ejecting the ball (retained gameplay run). The value, shown on the 2,000 to 10,000 inserts (lamps 60, 12, 28, 44, 59), is advanced by the top thumper and the spinner. The manual says the value resets to 2,000 when the ball enters the out-hole; in the retained runs the ROM keeps the lit value from ball to ball (4,000 through the first drain and 6,000 through the second of the game-over run) and returns it to 2,000 only when the credit button starts a game. The ROM runs the rule either way, so a recreation inherits it. The known-working script kicks it out at 110 degrees.
mechanisms.label: Top eject pocket (saucer)

mechanisms.behavior: A lane at the upper left with a roll-over switch (public 35) and a kicker coil (public 5, parts list `Kicker` J-28-2300) at its foot. When the switch closes the ROM scores the lane, 3,000 plus 2,000 for each letter of G-A-L-A-X-Y spotted (manual), and then pulses public 5 about four seconds later, driving the ball back up and out of the lane (retained gameplay run). The kicker-lane letter lamps (49 X, 33 Y, 50 G, 34 A, 18 L, 2 second A) show the letters spotted.
mechanisms.label: Upper-left kicker lane (kickback)

mechanisms.behavior: Four drop targets in one bank on the left side, top to bottom black (switch 9), yellow (10), blue (11) and red (4) (switch location drawing; IPDB `4-bank drop targets (1)`). A target's switch is closed while it is down. One reset coil (public 4, parts list `Drop Target Reset (1)` B-27-2300) raises the whole bank, and each target has its own knock-down coil (parts list `Drop Target Reset (Each Target) 4`): public 14 black, 13 yellow, 10 blue and 9 red. The ROM uses the knock-down coils to spot targets: the upper, middle and lower stand-up targets (switches 30, 29, 26) knock down the black, yellow and blue targets, and the return lanes knock down the red one (retained gameplay run; the feature text says the stand-ups spot the matching target). Home state is all four up. The ROM resets the bank at game start, after every drain and when the fourth target goes down; completing the bank advances the planet ladder (Mercury to Pluto, lamps 54, 38, 22, 6, 53, 37, 21 and 5 in the retained gameplay run).
mechanisms.label: Left four-target drop bank with individual knock-down coils

mechanisms.behavior: One spin target assembly (A-563-10) hangs across the opening below the eject pocket (switch location drawing). Each rotation closes its contact once; there is no coil or home sensor. It scores 100, 1,000 when its SPIN lamp (1) is lit, and advances the eject pocket value (manual).
mechanisms.label: Spinning target below the eject pocket

mechanisms.behavior: Three J-26-1200 thumper bumpers. The ROM fires each coil when its own switch closes and scores 1,000 on the 3-ball setting: switch 12 (top) fires public 3, switch 13 (lower right) public 7 and switch 14 (lower left) public 12 in the retained gameplay run. Printed solenoid numbers are 5, 4 and 10. The top bumper also advances the eject pocket value (manual).
mechanisms.label: Three thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two J-27-1700 slingshots, long ones along each side of the lower playfield. The ROM fires each coil when its switch closes and scores 10: switch 16 fires public 2 (left) and switch 15 public 1 (right) (retained gameplay run). Printed solenoid numbers are 1 and 2.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: One flipper on each side at the bottom of the playfield (IPDB `Flippers (2)`). Each coil is hard-wired through the contacts of the flipper enable relay to its side's cabinet button. The relay is public 19 (printed solenoid 15): the ROM raises it when a game starts and drops it on a tilt and at game over (retained runs). Each coil's end-of-stroke contact is closed at rest and opens at the end of the stroke to insert the hold winding. PinMAME publishes one callback per side (46 right, 48 left, with 45 and 47 alongside).
mechanisms.label: Two dual-winding flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Two gates with no coil or switch (playfield parts drawing): `BALL GATE A-104-R2` (callout 5), where the shooter lane meets the top arch, which lets the plunged ball out and keeps it from falling back, and `1-WAY GATE ASS'Y A-644` (callout 6, wire form 6A-257), a short wire at the left end of the top-lane group below the eject pocket's loop. They route the ball by its own motion; do not invent a powered diverter. The retained table models them as `Gate1` and `Gate2`.
mechanisms.label: Passive ball gates

physical.notes: Transformer-fed general illumination, switched by the general-illumination relay (public 17). The playfield wiring diagram draws `GEN. ILLUM` from A2J1-8 (W) at 6 VAC returning on A2J1-1 (R), the cabinet sheet draws `FRONT DOOR LITES` from A2J2-1 (Y-B) returning on A2J2-5 (G-R), and the general-use Transformer Schematic brings out `GEN. ILL. BUS` on A2J1-8, A2J2-1, A2J3-10 and A2J3-11 with `GEN. ILL. RETURN` on A2J2-5, A2J3-1 and A2J3-2. None of these sheets draws a relay contact in the circuit; the cabinet sheet draws only the `GEN. ILLUM. RELAY` coil, and no sheet shows which strings its contacts switch. The known-working script switches all of the table's general illumination, playfield and backglass, off while public 17 is on, and IPDB records the machine's computer-controlled general illumination. Bulb quantity and positions are not established.
